I'm a 54-year-old farmer with primary school education. I've been farming for 30 years here in Quzhou County. My farm is about 10 mu total. I have my wife, my son and daughter-in-law, and one grandchild at home — five people total. My son works off-farm at a factory in Handan, so he's only home for busy seasons. My daughter-in-law also does some part-time work in town. That means most days it's just me and my wife in the fields, though we get help from my son during wheat harvest and maize planting.

I grow wheat and maize on about 6 mu in a double-crop system, and I keep about 4 mu in cotton. The cotton brings decent cash, but it's heavy on labor with all the picking. Wheat and maize are more reliable — even if prices aren't great, I know I'll have grain to sell and some for home use.

This year, I'm thinking about what happened last year. The wheat did okay — I got about 420 jin per mu, but I spent too much on extra fertilizer because I got nervous. I won't make that mistake again. My neighbor Old Wang used a bit less nitrogen on his wheat and got almost the same yield, so I'm going to cut back slightly. For the 6 mu of wheat already in the ground from last fall, I put down base fertilizer already — about 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu. Now it's early spring, and when the wheat turns green in March, I'll topdress with about 12 kg of urea per mu. If it looks yellow at jointing, maybe I'll add another 5 kg, but I want to keep costs down. Total nitrogen should be around 16 kg per mu. I'll irrigate three times: green-up, jointing, and when the heads are filling. Pumping costs money, so I won't overdo it, but no water means no yield. I'll spray a herbicide once for weeds, and maybe an insecticide if I see aphids.

For summer maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in mid-June — the window is tight, maybe 5 or 6 days. I hire a combine for wheat harvest because my son can't do it all by hand, and then I plant maize immediately. I'll buy hybrid seed — about 3 kg per mu, costs roughly 60 yuan per mu. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting, then topdress urea at the big trumpet stage, about 18 kg nitrogen total per mu. I'll irrigate twice if it doesn't rain — seedling stage and trumpet stage. Yield should be around 450 kg per mu if the weather cooperates, similar to last year.

The 4 mu of cotton I'll plant in late April. I'll use saved seed from last year that seemed good. Cotton needs less fertilizer than people think — I'll put about 12 kg nitrogen per mu, split between base and flowering. I'll irrigate twice, at flowering and boll-setting. But cotton needs spraying for bollworm, that's for sure. I'll do herbicide and two insecticide sprays. The picking is the hard part — my wife and I will do most of it, but if the bolls open all at once I might hire a few days of labor. I expect about 250 kg per mu of seed cotton.

Money is always tight. My son sends some cash home, but I need to keep input costs around 5,000 yuan total. I can't afford to buy the "perfect" amount of everything, so I'd rather be a little conservative on fertilizer than run out of cash for pumping water or hiring the combine. That's my plan.
